upstream.title: Beyond Fresh Starts: Stateful Inference for Streaming ASR in Conversational Voice Agents

source_observations.problem: Fresh-start reset at every conversational turn discards useful acoustic context and disproportionately harms recognition at turn onsets; naive continuous state can instead retain harmful long-silence or backchannel context.
source_observations.baseline_fresh_start: Reset model state at the start of every turn.
source_observations.baseline_continuous_state: Carry streaming state continuously through inter-turn silence without manipulation.
source_observations.state_carry_over: Use the state at the end of one turn as the starting state for the next, bypassing inter-turn silence while preserving prior-turn context.
source_observations.state_rollback: Carry state across turns but, when the previous turn is shorter than a token threshold, roll back to the state saved after the last substantial turn to discard backchannel context.
source_observations.latency_scope: Authors report the qualitative ranking remains stable across supported low-latency settings below 250 ms and with Silero-VAD-derived turn boundaries on Switchboard.
source_observations.scope_note: These are upstream paper results, not Frankenstein measurements.

frankenstein_interpretation.candidate_role: ASR acoustic-state continuity policy between confirmed turns, orthogonal to canonical conversation memory and UnifiedDB.
frankenstein_interpretation.important_separation: Model acoustic cache is ephemeral inference state. It must not become canonical memory, identity state, or evidence authority.
frankenstein_interpretation.smallest_useful_delta_after_runner_recov: Add Fresh Start vs State Carry-over vs State Rollback as an A/B/C factor to the same pinned German room-audio ASR corpus after the existing target-runtime runner gate is resolved.
frankenstein_interpretation.safety_fence: Rollback/carry-over may affect ASR hypotheses only. It cannot mint a user fact, completed turn, VoiceIntent, tool request, world state or EffectGate authorization.

hypothesis: For a German-first local streaming ASR stack, preserving bounded cross-utterance acoustic state may reduce turn-onset errors without adding a second memory authority, provided short backchannels and long pauses trigger deterministic rollback/reset policy.
counterhypotheses: The gains may be architecture-specific to cache-aware FastConformer-RNNT and may not transfer to Qwen3-ASR or other current Trigger-7 candidates.
German room audio may contain speaker changes, reverberation and disfluencies that make carried acoustic state harmful or unstable.
A sufficiently strong fresh-start ASR model may make state management complexity unnecessary.
Cross-turn state may improve first-word WER while degrading contamination/recovery behavior, so aggregate WER alone is insufficient.
